Hospital Readmissions Explorer

A conversational interface for exploring public Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program data and making an analytical workflow easier to inspect.

Question Concept Prototype Validation Pilot Production
Central question

Can a conversational interface make a complex public quality dataset easier to explore without hiding the analytical structure?

Current state

A working web-interface prototype can accept questions and return data-driven responses.

Latest update

A deployment pipeline and custom web interface were assembled for interactive HRRP exploration.

Next experiment

Clarify guardrails, evaluation criteria, and the questions the interface should and should not answer.

Known limits: This is an exploratory interface, not clinical decision support. No claims of validation, completeness, or production readiness are made.

Exploring Simulation methodology

Flux Estimand Framework

An experimental methodology for structuring Flux simulations around explicit decisions, counterfactual comparisons, and the minimum model needed to estimate their consequences.

Question Concept Prototype Validation Pilot Production
Central question

How can simulation projects be organized around the causal consequences of a decision rather than an open-ended attempt to reproduce an entire domain?

Current state

A public methodology repository contains conceptual documentation, reusable agent guidance, and a template for downstream estimand projects; it does not contain an executable ModelBundle or its own completed estimand.

Latest update

The framework was organized around a reusable project template, an authoritative ESTIMAND.md specification, and agent guidance for creating and reviewing downstream projects.

Next experiment

Apply the framework to a concrete downstream decision problem and evaluate whether it produces a clearer, more defensible simulation specification.

Known limits: The methodology is experimental. The repository does not demonstrate an implemented estimand, executable simulation, empirical validation, downstream adoption, or improved decision outcomes.

Looking forMethodological feedback from simulation modelers and causal-inference practitioners

02 / Method

Building is part of the reasoning.

A prototype creates something concrete enough for users, experts, evidence, and constraints to push against.

  1. 01

    Observe

    Identify a recurring analytical problem or workflow that should work better.

  2. 02

    Reason

    Clarify the question, assumptions, users, evidence, and underlying structure.

  3. 03

    Prototype

    Build a working version quickly enough to make the idea tangible.

  4. 04

    Test

    Put it in front of users, experts, data, and real constraints.

  5. 05

    Evolve

    Improve it, pause it, publish what was learned, or develop it further.

03 / AI’s role

Faster implementation changes which ideas are feasible.

AI-assisted development can reduce the distance between a well-reasoned concept and a working interface. That means analytical work can begin with something people can test, rather than months of specifications alone.

What accelerates

  • interface and workflow implementation
  • exploration of alternative system designs
  • creation of testable analytical artifacts
  • iteration between reasoning and use

What does not disappear

  • statistical reasoning and domain expertise
  • definitions, assumptions, and data quality
  • review, validation, governance, and accountability
  • judgment about whether a problem is worth solving

AI is a force multiplier for rigorous analytical thinking—not a substitute for it.

04 / Philosophy

Structure Before Sophistication

Sophisticated-looking outputs are becoming easier to generate. Framing, definitions, assumptions, architecture, and validation are not.

Poor thinking can now be implemented faster, too. Structure is the quality-control layer: the disciplined design that makes an analytical system transparent, reproducible, maintainable, and defensible.

Clear questionsKnow what the system is meant to answer.
Defensible logicMake metrics and assumptions open to review.
Reproducible systemsBuild work that can be understood and repeated.
Honest boundariesState uncertainty and limits alongside capability.

06 / About

A statistician’s lab for analytical systems.

CentralStatz was founded by Alex Zajichek, a statistician and data scientist in Central Wisconsin with more than a decade of experience learning, teaching, and doing data science work across tools, methods, and problem contexts.

His work is especially grounded in healthcare, where messy systems, consequential decisions, and fragile metrics make sound analytical structure essential. Through the lab, Alex explores, designs, prototypes, and evaluates systems that make complex analytical questions easier to engage with—and easier to scrutinize.

Alex Zajichek · Statistician & data scientist · Wausau, Wisconsin
